analysis:
Examined ServingReadiness.swift (head 9-140), ProviderLogger.swift (head 149) and ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head 429-432).

ServingReadiness is a provider-local diagnostic. It also feeds the re-registration trigger (ProviderLoop.superviseServingAuthorization, not supplied). The changes are:
- a new .unconfirmed verdict for a refusal older than refusalMaxAge=60s (head 120-121);
- a request routed after the latest trust status now counts as .authorized (head 79-81, 115, 129-135);
- a refusal inside the 90s grace period is now .pending (head 117-118).

None of this grants authorization. Per TB-002/TB-011/T-053, the coordinator enforces serving authorization at shared routing and final handoff (authorizeInferenceHandoff). A local verdict cannot admit a connection, extend an App Attest lease or alter coordinator trust. Explicit untrusted/offline statuses and expired App Attest leases still block before the routed/unconfirmed logic (head 91-113).

The new noteCoordinatorRequest() hook on .inferenceRequest (Serve.swift 429-432) records only arrival time. It does not affect decryption or the inference path. Provider and operator are adversarial (ADV-001), but a forged local state file only misleads the operator's own diagnostics.

The new log case (Logger head 149) is a fixed string with no associated values. It preserves the closed public-log vocabulary (T-058 log-leak concern).

Remaining integration questions (availability only, A-018/T-057):
- How does superviseServingAuthorization treat .unconfirmed versus .blocked? If .unconfirmed suppresses re-registration indefinitely after a stale refusal, a truly unrouted legacy connection might never re-register. If it counts as blocked, behavior is unchanged.
- noteCoordinatorRequest and the lastRequestAt persistence/ordering relative to trust.receivedAt were not supplied. Clock/order assumptions should be checked.

These are availability concerns, not confidentiality or authorization ones. No security regression was identified in the supplied units.
